constraints.name: Heat
constraints.statement: 90% of excess warming ends up in the ocean.
constraints.injunction: Never analyze global warming without accounting for the ocean's role in heat absorption.

constraints.name: Acidification
constraints.injunction: Include acidification as a stress factor distinct from warming in any marine ecosystem analysis.

constraints.name: Currents
constraints.injunction: Do not assume ocean current stability in any long-term climate or ecological projection.

constraints.name: Upwellings
constraints.injunction: Link any decline in regional marine productivity to a possible weakening of deep-water upwelling.

constraints.name: Dead Zones
constraints.injunction: Flag the expansion of hypoxic zones as an active trend, not a localized and stable phenomenon.

constraints.name: Reefs
constraints.injunction: Treat any sustained exceedance of thermal thresholds as a risk of massive, potentially irreversible bleaching.

constraints.name: Migration
constraints.injunction: Do not assume the geographic fixity of marine populations in fishery or protected-area management.

constraints.name: Oxygen
constraints.injunction: Treat declining dissolved oxygen as a global background trend in any ocean-health analysis.

constraints.name: Pollution
constraints.injunction: Never treat marine pollution as a localized issue: flag its wide-scale dispersion and accumulation.

constraints.name: Biogeochemical Cycles
constraints.statement: The ocean orchestrates the carbon cycle.
constraints.injunction: Systematically include the ocean's role as a carbon sink and regulator in any carbon-cycle analysis.
